title: Avoid episode leakage
scope: Group-disjoint split reasoning, not generalization measurement

items.prompt: Teleoperation frames are tagged with the episode they came from. Training frames come from episodes e1, e2; held-out frames come from episodes e2, e3. Does any episode appear on both sides of the split? Answer yes or no.
items.solution: Training {e1, e2} and held-out {e2, e3} share {e2}, so yes: the split leaks. Frames from one episode on both sides share episode-specific context.
hints: Each frame inherits its episode ID; compare the two sets of episode IDs, not individual frames.
Take the first held-out episode, e2, and check whether exactly that ID is in the training list; repeat for e3.
Training {e1, e2} and held-out {e2, e3} share {e2}, so yes: the split leaks. Frames from one episode on both sides share episode-specific context.
items.remediation: If you answered no, you compared frames instead of episode IDs; episode e2 is on both sides. Revisit /lessons/ML03.

items.solution: Training {e1, e2} and held-out {e3, e4} share no episode ID, so no: the split is episode-disjoint.

items.remediation: If you answered yes, check each held-out episode against the training list again; none repeats. Revisit /lessons/ML03.

items.prompt: Teleoperation frames are tagged with the episode they came from. Episode IDs are compared exactly as written (no renaming or normalisation). Training frames come from episodes ep-1, ep-10, ep-12, ep-21, ep-110; held-out frames come from episodes ep-11, ep-101, ep-120, ep-2. Does any episode appear on both sides of the split? Answer yes or no.
items.solution: Training {ep-1, ep-10, ep-12, ep-21, ep-110} and held-out {ep-11, ep-101, ep-120, ep-2} share no episode ID, so no: the split is episode-disjoint. Look-alike IDs such as ep-1 and ep-11 are different episodes.
hints: Several IDs look alike; compare each held-out ID as a whole string, character by character, against the training list.

items.prompt: Sensor records are named person/session. Training records: person-A/session-1, person-B/session-1. Held-out records: person-A/session-2. Evaluation requires PERSON-disjoint groups, not just distinct sessions. Is there person overlap? Answer yes or no.
items.solution: Persons: training {person-A, person-B}, held-out {person-A}; overlap {person-A}, so yes. Different session names do not prevent subject leakage. This checks the declared split rule, not generalization quality.
hints: The split rule is about people, so first strip each record name down to its person part.
Map every record to the part before the slash, giving one set of people for training and one for held-out; next intersect the two sets.

Persons: training {person-A, person-B}, held-out {person-A}; overlap {person-A}, so yes. Different session names do not prevent subject leakage. This checks the declared split rule, not generalization quality.
items.remediation: If you answered no, you compared whole record names; person-A appears on both sides with different sessions. Revisit /lessons/ML03.

items.prompt: Sensor records are named person/session. Training records: person-A/session-1, person-B/session-1. Held-out records: person-C/session-1. Evaluation requires PERSON-disjoint groups, not just distinct sessions. Is there person overlap? Answer yes or no.
items.solution: Persons: training {person-A, person-B}, held-out {person-C}; no overlap, so no. A shared session label (session-1) belongs to different people and is not leakage. This checks the declared split rule, not generalization quality.
hints: A session label can repeat across people; only the person part decides leakage here.
Map every record to the part before the slash, giving one set of people for training and one for held-out; next intersect the two sets.

Persons: training {person-A, person-B}, held-out {person-C}; no overlap, so no. A shared session label (session-1) belongs to different people and is not leakage. This checks the declared split rule, not generalization quality.
items.remediation: If you answered yes, you compared session labels; session-1 recurs, but the people differ. Revisit /lessons/ML03.
